findings.title: Dark Web Profile: NightSpire Ransomware
findings.summary_md: SOCRadar's dark web profile describes NightSpire as a financially motivated ransomware group that emerged in early 2025 and runs a double extortion model, encrypting victim data and threatening to publish it on the group's dark web leak site if ransoms are not paid. The profile notes wide targeting of organizations across multiple sectors.

findings.title: NightSpire Ransomware: How It Works and How to Defend Against It
findings.summary_md: Proven Data's NightSpire analysis documents stolen data being transferred to attacker-controlled infrastructure with WinSCP, MEGACmd, or Rclone before a Go-based encryption payload obfuscated with RC4 and XOR is deployed. The writeup also describes extended sleep intervals between encryption operations to avoid real-time detection and log manipulation on the victim's systems.

findings.title: Decoding NightSpire: Ransomware IOCs Aren't Set in Stone
findings.summary_md: Huntress walks through an incident linked to the NightSpire ransomware workflow and uses it to show why indicators of compromise shift under a ransomware-as-a-service structure. The post argues the affiliate model means fixed IOC lists for the NightSpire brand go stale quickly.

findings.title: NightSpire Ransomware Attack Chain, Tools and Tactics
findings.summary_md: Picus Security counts at least 64 organizations across 33 countries hit by NightSpire between March and June 2025, with the United States leading the victim list ahead of Turkey, Hong Kong, Japan, Taiwan, Mexico, Spain, and Egypt. The analysis describes a Go-based encryptor paired with data theft before encryption and threats to publish stolen files on a Tor-based leak site.
